title: MINI-CHALLENGE: Complete Ship Diagnostic Data Model

story.setup: MENTOR-9: "Time to combine everything. Create a complex diagnostic report using scalars, lists, and dictionaries together. Real-world data is nested and complex—show me you can model our ship's complete state."
story.requirements: Build a comprehensive ship diagnostic data model that integrates ALL Section 1.2 concepts: scalars, lists, dictionaries, access patterns, and naming conventions.
story.success: MENTOR-9: "Impressive! That's a complete data model of our ship's state. Your memory banks are fully operational. Now let's verify data integrity with assertions."

description: Create a complete ship diagnostic system that integrates ALL Section 1.2 concepts: scalar variables, list variables, dictionary variables, access patterns, and naming rules.
requirements: Use all three variable types: scalar (${...}), list (@{...}), and dictionary (&{...})
Store ship name as scalar variable
Create list of at least 5 damaged components
Create dictionary of at least 5 system statuses (key=value pairs)
Access and log specific values from list (first item, last item, specific index)
Access and log specific values from dictionary (by key)
Use both *** Variables *** section AND keyword-based variable creation
Use Set Variable, Create List, and Create Dictionary keywords
Include both Log and Log Many/Log Dictionary for proper display
constraints: All three variable types must be present
Minimum 5 items in damaged systems list
Minimum 5 key-value pairs in system status dictionary
At least 3 scalar variables (ship name, diagnostic ID, timestamp)
Must access list items by index ([0], [-1], [2])
Must access dictionary values by key ([key])
Variables must follow naming conventions (mix of snake_case, UPPER_CASE)
Both file-level (*** Variables ***) and test-level variable creation required
instructions: Create '*** Test Cases ***' section with test named 'Complete Ship Diagnostic Data Model'
In the test, create ${timestamp} with Set Variable using value '2157-03-15 14:23:47 UTC'
Create @{damaged_systems} with Create List containing exactly these 5 items:
Access and log the first damaged system using ${damaged_systems}[0]
Access and log the last damaged system using ${damaged_systems}[-1]
Access and log the third damaged system using ${damaged_systems}[2]
Create &{system_status} with Create Dictionary containing exactly these 5 pairs:
Access and log Navigation status using ${system_status}[Navigation]
Access and log LifeSupport status using ${system_status}[LifeSupport]
Use Log Many to display all damaged systems with label 'Damaged Components:'
Use Log Dictionary to display the complete system status dictionary

Create a final summary log combining scalar, list, and dict values: 'Diagnostic complete for ${SHIP_NAME} at ${timestamp} - ${damaged_systems}[0] requires immediate attention - Navigation: ${system_status}[Navigation]'
hints: *** Variables *** section comes before *** Test Cases ***
Scalar variables: ${name}, List variables: @{list}, Dictionary variables: &{dict}
Use ${...} when accessing list items or dict values (not @{...} or &{...})
Create List takes items separated by 4 spaces
Create Dictionary uses key=value format (no spaces around =)
Log Many displays list items, Log Dictionary displays dict pairs
You can embed variable values in strings: 'Text ${variable} more text'
Mix naming styles: ${CONSTANTS} in uppercase, ${local_vars} in snake_case
First damaged system is at index [0], last at [-1], third at [2]
Dictionary keys ARE case-sensitive: 'Navigation' ≠ 'navigation' (string keys, not variable names)

theory.title: Section 1.2 Mini-Challenge: Data Modeling and Integration
theory.content:
MENTOR-9 brings up a holographic ship schematic with glowing data points.

"PROTO-7, you've learned the three fundamental data types. Now combine them into something real—a complete diagnostic model of our ship's state. Scalars, lists, dictionaries, all working together."

What This Challenge Tests

ConceptWhere It AppearsWhy It Matters
Scalar Variables ${SHIP_NAME}, ${timestamp} Single values: IDs, names, timestamps
List Variables @{damaged_systems} Ordered collections of related items
Dictionary Variables &{system_status} Structured key-value data
List Access ${list}[0], ${list}[-1] Extract specific items by position
Dictionary Access ${dict}[key] Query structured data by name
Variable Naming UPPER_CASE, snake_case Consistency and readability
*** Variables *** Section File-level constants Reusable values across tests
Keywords Set/Create Variable/List/Dict Dynamic data creation

Real-World Application

This challenge mirrors actual test automation scenarios:

  • System health monitoring - Track multiple component states
  • API response modeling - Store complex JSON-like structures
  • Test data organization - Scalars for config, lists for iterations, dicts for structured data
  • Diagnostic reporting - Combine multiple data types into comprehensive reports

Professional Patterns You're Implementing:

1. Data Type Selection
  • Scalars for unique identifiers: Ship name, timestamp, version
  • Lists for collections: Damaged systems, error logs, test cases
  • Dictionaries for mappings: System statuses, configuration, metadata
2. Hierarchical Data Modeling
*** Variables ***
${SHIP_NAME}    Starlight Explorer    # Top-level identifier

*** Test Cases ***
Diagnostic Model
    @{systems}     Create List    Nav    Power    Life Support    # Collection
    &{status}      Create Dictionary    Nav=OK    Power=FAIL      # Mapping
    
    # Access specific data
    Log    Ship ${SHIP_NAME} - First system: ${systems}[0] - Status: ${status}[Nav]

This creates a three-tier data model:

  1. Constants: ${SHIP_NAME} (file-level, unchanging)
  2. Collections: @{systems} (ordered list of components)
  3. Mappings: &{status} (component → status lookup)
3. Variable Scope Strategy
ScopeWhen to UseExample
*** Variables *** Constants, config, shared values ${API_URL}, ${SHIP_NAME}
Test-level (Set Variable) Dynamic values, test-specific data ${timestamp}, ${response}
Keyword-level Temporary calculations, intermediate values ${temp}, ${result}
4. Access Patterns for Complex Data
*** Test Cases ***
Access Patterns
    @{items}    Create List    A    B    C    D    E
    &{data}     Create Dictionary    status=OK    code=200
    
    # List access patterns
    ${first}    Set Variable    ${items}[0]      # First item
    ${last}     Set Variable    ${items}[-1]     # Last item
    ${third}    Set Variable    ${items}[2]      # Specific item
    
    # Dictionary access patterns
    ${status}   Set Variable    ${data}[status]  # By key
    ${code}     Set Variable    ${data}[code]    # By key
    
    # Combined in output
    Log    Status: ${status}, Code: ${code}, First: ${first}, Last: ${last}

Why Combine All Three Types?

Real Example: API Test Result Storage

*** Variables ***
${API_BASE}         https://api.example.com
${TEST_ID}          diagnostic-2157-03-15

*** Test Cases ***
API Diagnostic
    # Scalar: Test metadata
    ${timestamp}        Set Variable    2157-03-15 14:23:47 UTC
    
    # List: Endpoints to test
    @{endpoints}        Create List    /health    /status    /metrics    /users    /admin
    
    # Dictionary: Expected status codes
    &{expected}         Create Dictionary    health=200    status=200    metrics=200    users=401    admin=403
    
    # Access: First endpoint to test
    ${first_endpoint}   Set Variable    ${endpoints}[0]
    Log                 Testing ${API_BASE}${first_endpoint}
    
    # Access: Expected status for health endpoint
    ${expected_code}    Set Variable    ${expected}[health]
    Log                 Expected status: ${expected_code}
    
    # Combined summary
    Log                 Test ${TEST_ID} at ${timestamp} - Checking ${first_endpoint} (expect ${expected_code})

Output:

Testing https://api.example.com/health
Expected status: 200
Test diagnostic-2157-03-15 at 2157-03-15 14:23:47 UTC - Checking /health (expect 200)

Naming Convention Strategies

ConventionUse CaseExample
UPPER_CASE Constants (*** Variables *** section) ${SHIP_NAME}, ${API_URL}
snake_case Local variables, dynamic values ${first_damage}, ${system_status}
descriptive_names Complex data structures @{damaged_systems}, &{crew_roster}

Data Flow Pattern

*** Variables ***
${CONFIG}           MyApp v2.0    # 1. Define constants

*** Test Cases ***
Data Flow Demo
    # 2. Create dynamic data
    ${time}          Set Variable    14:23:47
    @{errors}        Create List     ERR-001    ERR-002    ERR-003
    &{severity}      Create Dictionary    ERR-001=HIGH    ERR-002=LOW    ERR-003=MEDIUM
    
    # 3. Access specific values
    ${first_error}   Set Variable    ${errors}[0]
    ${severity_1}    Set Variable    ${severity}[ERR-001]
    
    # 4. Combine in output
    Log              ${CONFIG} at ${time}: First error ${first_error} has severity ${severity_1}

Output:

MyApp v2.0 at 14:23:47: First error ERR-001 has severity HIGH

Success Criteria

Your diagnostic data model is successful if:

  1. ✅ *** Variables *** section with constants (${SHIP_NAME}, ${DIAGNOSTIC_VERSION})
  2. ✅ Scalar variable created with Set Variable (${timestamp})
  3. ✅ List variable with 5+ items created with Create List
  4. ✅ Dictionary variable with 5+ pairs created with Create Dictionary
  5. ✅ List access by index: [0] (first), [-1] (last), [2] (third)
  6. ✅ Dictionary access by key: [Navigation], [LifeSupport]
  7. ✅ Log Many displays list contents
  8. ✅ Log Dictionary displays dict contents
  9. ✅ Final summary combines all three data types
  10. ✅ Proper variable naming conventions used
  11. ✅ Test passes without errors
  12. ✅ Output clearly shows ship diagnostic state

Common Patterns in Production Code

Pattern 1: Configuration Management

*** Variables ***
${ENV}              staging
@{REGIONS}          us-east-1    eu-west-1    ap-south-1
&{ENDPOINTS}        api=https://api.staging.com    web=https://staging.com

*** Test Cases ***
Deploy Check
    ${region}       Set Variable    ${REGIONS}[0]
    ${api_url}      Set Variable    ${ENDPOINTS}[api]
    Log             Checking ${ENV} in ${region}: ${api_url}

Pattern 2: Test Result Aggregation

*** Test Cases ***
Result Collection
    ${test_name}    Set Variable    Login Flow Test
    @{steps}        Create List    Navigate    Enter Creds    Submit    Verify
    &{results}      Create Dictionary    Navigate=PASS    Enter Creds=PASS    Submit=FAIL    Verify=SKIP
    
    ${failed_step}  Set Variable    ${steps}[2]
    ${status}       Set Variable    ${results}[Submit]
    
    Log             Test: ${test_name} - Failed at step '${failed_step}' with status ${status}

Pattern 3: Nested Data Structures

*** Test Cases ***
Nested Model
    @{admins}       Create List    alice@example.com    bob@example.com
    @{users}        Create List    charlie@example.com    diana@example.com
    &{access}       Create Dictionary    admins=${admins}    users=${users}
    
    ${first_admin}  Set Variable    ${access}[admins][0]
    Log             First admin: ${first_admin}

MENTOR-9 steps back, arms crossed. "This is your memory mastery test, PROTO-7. Build a complete ship diagnostic data model."

"Use scalars for metadata, lists for damaged systems, dictionaries for status mappings. Access specific values from each. Show me you can handle complex, real-world data structures."

She gestures to the editor. "When this diagnostic is complete, we'll have a full picture of our ship's state. Begin."

Dictionary variable with exactly 5 key-value pairs
Log Many used to display list contents
Log Dictionary used to display dictionary contents
Final summary log combining scalar, list, and dict values
Proper naming conventions (UPPER_CASE constants, snake_case locals)
